oneLiner: The only wafer-scale inference platform running in production at scale, sold mostly as a cloud service to a handful of anchor customers. The market is betting on one number: whether the contracted backlog converts into the promised 2027 revenue step-up while OpenAI stays the anchor rather than drifting back to Nvidia.

verdict.summary: After the October reset the stock prices something close to our base case: 2027 core revenue roughly 2.6x 2026 at a ~10x EV/Sales, not management's 'more than triple'. That leaves a roughly symmetric, wide distribution - the bull case (the triple lands, 14x) is worth ~60% more, the bear case (OpenAI shifts incremental work to Nvidia, growth stalls near +70%) roughly half. The losses and burn are not the issue while ~$8.6B of liquidity lasts; customer concentration and the speed of the owned-capacity margin inflection are. We would turn Positive on a Q3 print that holds RPO near $25B with a Q4 guide implying ~$265M+ of core revenue, and Cautious if OpenAI's share of the order book visibly shrinks.
wtb: FY2027 core revenue reaches at least ~$2.3B (about 2.6x the ~$885M FY2026 guide midpoint), with the first 2027 framework due at the Q4 report (~Feb/Mar 2027).
RPO stays at or above ~$25B at Q3 (Nov 12, 2026): new bookings at least replace what converts, and OpenAI's 750MW commitment is not resized.
Owned data centers lift core gross margin back to 43%+ by Q1 2027 from the 38-40% Q3 guide, showing the capex (127% of TTM revenue) earns a return.
The market pays ~10x EV/Sales at end-2027 for a business still growing 50%+ into 2028.

bear.why: OpenAI keeps its contracted floor but routes new high-speed modes to Nvidia; RPO stops growing, capacity arrives late and 2027 core revenue grows only ~70% to ~$1.5B. Margins stay below 40% on leased capacity, so the market values it as a concentrated, sub-scale hardware-and-hosting vendor.

base.why: Most of the 600MW+ of contracted capacity is live by late 2027; OpenAI ramps, AWS Bedrock (Q1 2027) and the AMD partnership broaden the base, and core revenue reaches ~$2.3B (~2.6x). Gross margin recovers to the low-40s on owned systems but GAAP losses persist, holding the multiple near 10x.

bull.why: The 'more than triple' plan lands (~$3.0B), RPO compounds past $25B on new frontier-lab and enterprise contracts, and core operating margin approaches breakeven. Fast inference becomes a recognised category with Cerebras as the non-Nvidia standard, earning a premium growth multiple.

scenarioModel.note: Revenue is core revenue (GAAP plus customer-warrant amortization, less pass-through), the basis of company guidance; GAAP revenue runs lower by the warrant amortization. Value per share = (rev x EV/Sales + current net cash) / current shares, so the page uses today's net cash; by end-2027 cumulative capex and burn will reduce it, a further drag in the bear case. Multiples are applied to FY2027 core revenue at end-2027. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Does OpenAI stay the anchor, or drift back to Nvidia?
debates.bull: OpenAI committed to up to 750MW over three years (Jan 2026), and Altman publicly called Cerebras 'a close partner' after the October scare; RPO of $25.4B is contracted, not pipeline.
debates.bear: SemiAnalysis reported (Sep 30, 2026) that OpenAI's newest Ultrafast mode runs on Nvidia GPUs; a large share of RPO is tied to OpenAI, and Nvidia's $20B Groq deal gives it a fast-inference answer.
debates.view: The contracted floor makes a collapse unlikely, but the multiple depends on OpenAI expanding, not merely honouring, the deal. Concentration is the single biggest swing factor between the bear and base cases.

signpost.metric: RPO and any update on OpenAI deployed / contracted MW
signpost.threshold: RPO at or above $25B with OpenAI capacity on schedule = base holds; RPO down or OpenAI resized = bear

debates.q: Is growth decelerating, or pausing before the capacity step-up?
debates.bull: Core revenue grew 103% in Q2 2026 and core cloud +287%; the FY2026 guide was raised, and 600MW+ of capacity live or contracted by end-2027 is what supports a 2027 triple.
debates.bear: GAAP revenue growth slowed from +94% to +74% YoY and fell ~7% QoQ in Q2; core hardware grew only 17%, and the Q3 core guide ($214-216M) is barely above Q2.
debates.view: The deceleration is capacity-gated, not demand-gated, if the Q4 step-up shows up. The FY2026 guide implies Q4 core revenue of roughly $260-275M (Siberforge estimate from the guide midpoint); missing that would mean the 2027 plan is at risk.

signpost.metric: Q3 core revenue vs $214-216M guide; Q4 core revenue guide
signpost.threshold: Q4 guide at or above ~$265M = on track for base or bull; below $240M = bear

debates.q: When does the capex start earning a return?
debates.bull: Leased third-party capacity is the temporary cost; owned, lower-cost systems come online in Q4 2026, and core gross margin was already 40.6% in Q2 (+940bp YoY).
debates.bear: TTM capex is 127% of revenue and free cash flow -$905M; GAAP operating loss was 2.6x revenue in Q2 (mostly $377M of IPO stock comp) and ~$1.13B of warrant assets will depress GAAP revenue for years.
debates.view: Liquidity of ~$8.6B covers years of burn, so this is a valuation issue, not a solvency one. The test is whether core gross margin turns up as owned capacity arrives; if not, the cloud model is a low-margin hosting business.

signpost.metric: Core gross margin and core operating margin
signpost.threshold: core GM back above 43% and core op margin better than -15% by Q1 2027 = bullish; GM stuck below 40% = bearish

thesis: Architecturally different, not a GPU clone. Wafer-scale SRAM keeps model weights on-die, which wins on tokens per second for agentic and reasoning workloads, and needs no HBM or CoWoS - the two chokepoints every GPU vendor queues for.
The cloud business is the growth engine. Core cloud and services revenue overtook hardware in Q2 2026, turning lumpy system sales into recurring inference revenue.
Contracted visibility few small-caps have. RPO of $25.4B is about 29x FY2026 guided core revenue, and 600MW+ of data-center capacity is live or under contract for delivery by end-2027.
The October reset removed the hype premium. The base case is now roughly what the stock pays for, so the bull case (the triple lands) is not needed to avoid losses - only the base.

latestQuarter.label: Q2 FY2026 (ended Jun 30, 2026; reported Aug 12, 2026)
points: Core revenue $209.9M, +103% YoY (GAAP $180.1M, +74%), above the ~$194M guide.
Core cloud/services $127.7M (+287%) vs core hardware $82.1M (+17%); GAAP hardware $54.1M after $44.3M of customer-warrant amortization.

latestProse: Q2 FY2026 (ended Jun 30; reported Aug 12, the first full quarter as a public company). Core revenue of $209.9M rose 103% and beat the ~$194M guide, but the mix and the GAAP line set the tone: core cloud and services nearly quadrupled to $127.7M and overtook core hardware ($82.1M, +17%), while GAAP revenue of $180.1M carried $44.3M of customer-warrant amortization. Core gross margin reached 40.6% against 14.2% GAAP, and the core operating loss was a modest -$33.6M; the GAAP operating loss of $477M was mostly $377M of IPO stock comp. RPO reached $25.4B. The disclosure that matters most is structural: ~$1.13B of customer-warrant assets, the price of landing OpenAI and the UAE anchors, will amortize as contra-revenue for years, so GAAP will understate core revenue well into 2027.
guidanceProse: FY2026 raised across all metrics: core revenue $880-890M, core gross margin 41-43%, core operating margin -19% to -17%. Q3 guides sequentially weaker - core revenue $214-216M, gross margin 38-40%, operating margin -25% to -23% - because leased third-party capacity carries the ramp until owned systems come online in Q4. Management plans to more than triple revenue in 2027, with AMD-partnered disaggregated inference in production in Q4 2026, AWS Bedrock in Q1 2027, manufacturing capacity up more than 10x in 2026 (Flex, Sanmina, Rocket EMS) and TSMC wafer supply secured. Since the print: SemiAnalysis reported (Sep 30) that OpenAI's newest Ultrafast mode runs on Nvidia GPUs, Altman responded (Oct 2) that Cerebras is 'a close partner', and the post-IPO lock-up expired in early October (about 19.4M shares per secondary reports; exact dates unverified). Q3 results are scheduled for Nov 12, 2026, after the close.
segments: Cloud and inference services (core $127.7M in Q2 2026, ~61% of core revenue, +287%): tokens sold through Cerebras Cloud, OpenAI capacity and partner marketplaces (AWS Bedrock from Q1 2027).
Hardware systems (core $82.1M, ~39%, +17%): CS-3 systems for sovereign and research buyers; lumpy, and where warrant amortization hits GAAP revenue hardest.
Customers: OpenAI, G42, MBZUAI and AWS are named significant customers; FY2025 revenue was 86% UAE entities. Cognition, Lovable, Block, Figma, AlphaSense, GSK and CrowdStrike broaden the tail.
competitive: Nvidia is the default and bought Groq for $20B in Dec 2025 - a direct fast-inference response, and reportedly the hardware behind OpenAI's newest Ultrafast mode.
AMD is a partner rather than a rival here: wafer-scale integrated with Helios for disaggregated inference (vendor-claimed up to 5x throughput), in production Q4 2026.
Hyperscaler ASICs (TPU, Trainium, Maia) and Broadcom/Marvell custom silicon compete for the same inference budgets at the largest buyers.
Risk to the speed premium: commodity GPU token prices falling faster than customers will pay for latency.
moat: Wafer-scale SRAM is hard to replicate and demonstrably fast at inference, but the moat is narrow: one TSMC process with no second source, and Nvidia can buy or build fast inference while bundling an unmatched software ecosystem. The $25.4B RPO is the strongest moat evidence - if it converts and if the anchor customers keep expanding.
risks: Customer concentration. A large share of RPO is tied to OpenAI and FY2025 revenue was 86% UAE entities; the September SemiAnalysis report showed how fast a single routing decision at OpenAI reprices the stock.
Decelerating reported growth. GAAP revenue growth slowed from +94% to +74% YoY and dipped QoQ in Q2; if the Q4 step-up slips, the 2027 triple looks like a target rather than a plan.
Burn and capex intensity. TTM free cash flow -$905M with capex 127% of revenue; ~$8.6B of liquidity covers it for now, but a slower ramp means more years of burn and possible further financing.

GAAP losses and dilution. GAAP operating loss was 2.6x revenue in Q2 on IPO stock comp, ~$1.13B of warrant assets depress GAAP revenue for years, and ongoing stock comp plus customer warrants dilute holders.
Supply and competition. Single-source TSMC wafer dependency, and Nvidia-Groq competing for both demand and foundry priority.
catalysts: Oct 28-30, 2026: MSFT, GOOGL, META, AMZN Q3 calls - inference capex and any OpenAI capacity commentary (debate 1).
Nov 12, 2026 (confirmed, after close): Q3 2026 results - RPO, Q4 guide, core gross margin (debates 1, 2, 3).
Q4 2026: owned data centers come online; AMD disaggregated inference in production (debate 3).
Q1 2027: Cerebras on AWS Bedrock in production (debate 2).
~Feb/Mar 2027: Q4 2026 results and the first FY2027 revenue framework vs the 'more than triple' plan (debates 2, 3).

valPresets.note: Pre-scale company with three public quarters of history; TTM revenue uses GAAP (below core revenue by warrant amortization). Values the terminal business off a revenue path, horizon FCF margin and exit multiple; the reverse DCF needs ~73% a year revenue growth for 7 years, below the trailing track record.
